problem_summary.summary: Count the distinct ways to reach the top of a staircase when each move climbs either one or two steps.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: an integer n for the number of steps. Return the number of distinct ways to reach step n.

brute_force.explanation: Recursively count the ways after choosing a one-step move and a two-step move. This direct recurrence is useful for revealing the state relationship, but repeatedly solves the same remaining-step subproblems.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every valid path to the top ends with either a one-step move from n - 1 or a two-step move from n - 2. The recursive calls enumerate both disjoint cases, and negative remaining steps contribute no paths.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(2^n) — without caching, the recursion branches into overlapping subproblems.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary — the deepest recursion path has at most n calls.

optimized.explanation: Use the recurrence ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2), retaining only the two preceding counts instead of a full table.
optimized.correctness_idea: A final move to step n comes from exactly one of steps n - 1 or n - 2. These sets of paths are disjoint, so their counts add. The rolling variables preserve those two required counts at every iteration.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each step from 3 through n is processed once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — only two prior counts and one temporary count are stored.
